__________________________________________________________ Hon'ble Shri Justice Sachin Singh Rajput, Order on Board 15.06.2024

The driver and possession holder of the offending vehicle motorcycle bearing Registration No. CG 07 LL 4409 have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short MV Act) being aggrieved with the award dated 29.11.2016 passed in Claim Case No. 136/2013 by the learned 6th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Durg C.G.
2.

entities.text: 6th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Durg
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
While partly allowing an application filed under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 11,45,000/- in favour of Respondents No.1 to 6/claimants on account of death of deceased Poornanad in an accident that occurred on 21.03.2013 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle motorcycle Neutral Citation bearing registration No. CG 07 LL 4409 driven by Appellant No. 1/Nilesh Kumar (Minor), which was in possession of Appellant No.2/Smt.
Sangeeta and Respondent No.7/Suraj Singh Bhuwal was the registered owner.

3. On the basis of material available on record, the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation as stated above, however, held that the Appellants liable to pay the compensation and exonerated Respondent No.7 from its liability.

The only question requires determination by this Court as to whether Respondent No.7 who admittedly the registered owner of the offending vehicle could have also been held liable to pay the compensation.

4. Learned Counsel appearing for the Appellants submits that admittedly Respondent No.7 was the registered owner of the offending vehicle and in light of order passed by the Supreme Court in case of Naveen Kumar Vs. Vijay Kumar & ors., (2018) 3 SCC 1 there is no liability on the part of Appellants and Respondent No.7 is to pay the compensation.

Learned Counsel appearing for Respondent No.7 submits that though Respondent No.7 was the registered owner of the offending vehicle, however long back, the offending vehicle was sold to Appellant no.2 and the Appellant No.2 allowed the minor to drive the offending vehicle, therefore,
the Respondent No.7 can not be made liable to pay the compensation.
7.
In light of judgment of Supreme Court in the case of Dr. T.V. Jose Vs. Chacko P.M. @ Thankachan & ors (2001) 8 SCC 748, Pushpa @ Leela and ors.

and ors. (2011) 2 SCC 240 and Naveen Kumar (Supra), admittedly Respondent No.7 was the registered owner of the offending vehicle, therefore, this appeal is allowed in part and Respondent No.7/Suraj Singh Bhuwal is also held liable to pay the compensation jointly or separately.
8. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part.
9. No cost.
